turns.spoken:
The sky appears blue thanks to a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering.

Sunlight is made up of all the colors of the rainbow. Our atmosphere is filled with tiny particles of air, like nitrogen and oxygen molecules. Scattering: When sunlight hits those tiny particles in the atmosphere, it gets scattered in different directions. Blue light scatters most. This means it scatters more easily off those tiny air molecules. Our eyes are more sensitive to blue light, so we see the scattered blue light as the sky's color.

So, the sky appears blue because blue light is scattered more effectively by the Earth's atmosphere.
